newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES MIXED IN SHORT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES MIXED IN SHORT MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened short on Monday with trading rates quoted stable to firmer in quiet trade, dealers said.
"The market is a bit short largely due to a lack of maturities but we expect it to be flush with money tomorrow (Tuesday) and possibly rates could come down," said one dealer.
On Monday, discount houses were buying central bank bills at 19.60 percent and selling them on the open market at 19.50 percent, both unchanged from Friday.

NCDs redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were also buying and selling steadily at 23 percent and 22.50 percent respectively but bankers acceptances edged up to 21 and 20.50 percent from 20.50 and 20 percent.
Call money added half a percentage point to 22.50 percent, with the central Reserve Bank putting the shortage figure at Z$35 million.
